_comment: Skill admission and refusal ledger (road-to-skill-estate-drawdown Phase 3). The five skill-growth questions from skill-writing/references/procedure.md 0b live HERE, not in a PR body: check_finding_dispositions.ts:11 rejects that surface for findings in its own words -- a comment is mutable and unaudited, it is transport, not a record. Read by src/scripts/check_skill_admissions.ts, FORWARD-ONLY: only skills added since the base ref need a row, so the 299 already in the tree are grandfathered by construction rather than by a list someone maintains. Fields on an `admitted` row: skill, decision, date, family, capability, why_not_extend, why_not_a_guideline, visibility. A `rejected` row needs skill, decision, date and `instead`, and must NOT name a skill that exists.

_absence_of_refusals: AC-5 asks for one historical refusal backfilled OR the absence of any recorded. The absence is recorded, because it is the finding: a grep for a refused skill proposal over archive/, later/ and stubs/ returns the recurring OBSERVATION that the count keeps climbing (road-to-capability-governance.md:46) and one 2026-05-01 audit that captured the count as data (road-to-governance-cleanup.md:64). No skill proposal was ever refused in a form the tree records -- which is exactly what a ledger kept in PR bodies would produce, and is the defect rather than a gap in this backfill. The first genuine `rejected` row will be the first visible no.

instead: Ships as a command routed through production-validator, which carries unscoped Bash and can invoke it deterministically. AI council 2/2: the evidence establishes a COVERAGE gap, not a SKILL-SHAPED gap -- a site-type-conditional config, 7 deterministic checks, 4 tiers, 18 schema tests and a hard pass/fail benchmark gate are the signature of a linter. `later/` was refused explicitly: parking implies the problem is timing or evidence, and it is neither. Reopen only on demonstrated failures in discovery, orchestration or interpretation that cannot be fixed in the validator or the command contract -- and cite THAT evidence, not the original 0-of-8 coverage gap. Recorded at road-to-web-launch-readiness b-estate-decision-web-launch.

family: design / asset authoring. It sits between `iconography` (the incumbent set answers first) and `image-generation` (a raster), and beside `logo-generation`, `canvas-design` and `wireframe`, which all produce hand-authored SVG and route into it rather than restating it.
capability: The procedure for writing or editing an SVG by hand, and the status vocabulary that binds a claim to evidence: read the delivery mode, classify the asset, write with the invariants, run the static witness, run the engine witness, look, and report `verified` only against a render manifest whose digest equals the delivered file's. Raster-to-vector is a named branch with a measured procedure rather than a look. Six lanes produced hand-authored SVG and none of them had any of this.
why_not_extend: Measured against the overlap scan, not asserted: no existing skill holds a hand-authored-SVG procedure, and the six producing lanes sit in three packs — `iconography`, `wireframe` and `design-intelligence` in frontend-design, `logo-generation` in ai-image, `canvas-design` in ai-video — plus one guideline. A reference file under any one of them is unreachable from the other two packs, while `packs:` takes a list, so the owner reaches all of them and a reference cannot. Recorded as decision E2 of road-to-svg-with-a-witness.
why_not_a_guideline: A guideline is read; this is executed. Its steps invoke two checkers and bind a status word to one of their outputs — `verified` requires a render manifest whose recorded digest equals the delivered file's digest on disk, which is a procedure with a falsifiable outcome rather than advice. The prose half of the same roadmap DID go to guidelines and authorities: the motion mechanisms to fe-design's § Motion, the ARIA rows to the accessibility corpus, the render-security sinks to that skill. Only the procedure is here.
visibility: Routed, not browsed. It ships `evals/triggers.json` with six should-trigger and six should-not-trigger queries whose near-misses are exactly the neighbours above, and the six lanes each carry a one-line pointer into it. The description is 130 characters and names the six jobs plus the two checks, so a host that shows only descriptions still routes it. Its catalogue line costs 32 tokens, paid back in the same change by trimming four lane descriptions: the per-spawn preamble payload measures 135,975 against a measured ceiling of 135,980.
estate_cost: skill_count 299 -> 300, claimed with estate_growth_exempt in the roadmap's own frontmatter; skill_description_tokens 11,460 -> 11,456, a net REDUCTION because the four lane descriptions were compressed by more than the new one costs.
